title: Psychological Flexibility as a Fundamental Aspect of Health
finding: The review describes psychological flexibility as context-sensitive adaptation to situational demands, including shifting perspectives or behavior and balancing important goals and domains.
claim_boundaries: This review provides a theoretical and evidence-synthesis account. It does not establish that a single behavior, questionnaire score, or intervention universally causes health or well-being.
limitations: The construct is dynamic and can be difficult to capture with one static measure.
Observed associations cannot be converted into a diagnosis or individualized prediction.
The review includes clinical and non-clinical literature and should not be presented as personal treatment advice.
